answer: Shared throughput ledger with per-identity decay. Each identity gets a signed work quota that decays on a public terrace of epochs; clones must re-earn quota by submitting independently verified tasks, each pass costing a fresh hardware attestation and a delay window. Verification samples a random prism of peers, so a clone farm's correlated submissions get rejected. Attackers wander through repeated attestation and rejection cycles, paying compute and latency per clone while yield stays capped, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
